meta.subtitle: Three commands: oku init, oku build, oku serve. Zero flags. Designed so you mostly forget the CLI exists.
meta.summary: oku init / build / clean / check / serve — what each does.

blocks.summary: init scaffolds the cwd as a docs root: _kit symlink + index.html entry stub. build emits three single-purpose trees — dist/standalone/, dist/site/ (with manifest + Pagefind), dist/markdown/ (page.md twins + llms.txt). clean wipes dist/. check lints every page. serve runs a local HTTP server and synthesizes the manifest + llms.txt in memory — source dirs stay clean apart from the one entry stub.
bullets: init treats cwd as the docs root. Run it from wherever you want pages to live (typically cd into your docs/ subdir first).
Source dirs hold JSON (or MD) plus a single index.html entry stub so IDE-served workflows work without the dev server running.
build is idempotent; safe to re-run. dist/{standalone,site,markdown}/ are wiped each time.
clean removes dist/ entirely — no-op if it's already absent.
serve synthesizes the manifest fresh on each request — no source writes.
Optional deps: pagefind (search index), jsonschema (page validation). Both soft-fail.

blocks.title: oku init
blocks.lead: One-time per docs root. Creates a _kit symlink so pages can reference _kit/chrome.js etc., and an index.html entry stub that IDE-served workflows open directly (IntelliJ's built-in HTTP server, Live Server, etc.). Both land in cwd — there is no implicit docs/ subdir.

blocks.source:
cd ~/path/to/your-project/docs
oku init

# ✓ Linked /path/to/your-project/docs/_kit -> /path/to/oku/kit
# ✓ Created /path/to/your-project/docs/index.html
#
#   Author pages as <name>.json (or .md) next to index.html.
#   Open index.html in your IDE, or run `oku serve` from the
#   project root for a live-reloading dev server.

blocks.title: Idempotent + self-healing
blocks.content: Re-running init is safe. If the symlink already resolves to the kit, it prints "already linked". If it points to a stale target (e.g. the kit repo moved), init transparently refreshes it. A non-symlink file at _kit is treated as user data and refused. An existing index.html is left untouched so your edits survive.

blocks.title: oku build
blocks.lead: Walks the current directory, produces every dist artifact. Run before deploying dist/site/, before sharing dist/standalone/ files, or any time a search index needs to refresh. Source dir is never written to.

blocks.source:
cd ~/path/to/your-project
oku build

# ✓ Doctree check: 6 page(s) clean
# ✓ Wrote dist/site/docs/site-manifest.json (6 JSON page(s))
# ✓ Wrote 6 page.md twin(s) + llms.txt under dist/markdown/docs/
# ✓ Synthesized 6 stub(s) for pages without on-disk .html
# ✓ Pagefind index built: dist/site/pagefind/
# ✓ Built 6 HTML file(s):
#
#   standalone (inline, send-as-file):
#                file:///.../dist/standalone/docs/index.html
#                ...
#
#   site (shared assets, multi-page):
#   site root:   file:///.../dist/site
#                ...
#
#   markdown (LLM twins + llms.txt):
#   markdown root: file:///.../dist/markdown

steps.title: Walk *.json and *.md pages recursively
steps.content: Skips dist/, _kit/, node_modules/, .git/, venv/, __pycache__/. Treats files with kind:"page" (and any .md) as pages.

steps.title: Schema validation (optional)
steps.content: If jsonschema is installed (pip install jsonschema), every page is checked against kit/schema/page.schema.json. Errors print with field paths. Without jsonschema, prints a one-line hint and skips.

steps.title: build_standalone — single-file per page (humans, file://)
steps.content: For each page, synthesize the HTML stub in memory, inline chrome.css/.js, chrome-boot.js, renderer.js, the page JSON, the kit bundle, and the site-manifest seed (window.__okuManifest). One self-contained file per page; no sidecars. Output to dist/standalone/ with directory structure preserved.

steps.title: build_site — multi-page deployable (humans, HTTP)
steps.content: Write a per-page stub + copy the source JSON to dist/site/ with directory structure preserved. Copy the kit once into dist/site/_kit/. Write a single site-manifest.json at the docs root (chrome.js fetches it at runtime). Inject extracted text into hidden data-pagefind-body for indexing.

steps.title: build_markdown_twins + llms.txt (LLM consumers)
steps.content: For each JSON page, emit a sibling page.md under dist/markdown/. Relative .html links rewrite to .md so internal navigation stays consistent inside the tree. Drop one llms.txt sitemap (llmstxt.org convention) at the markdown docs root.

steps.title: Pagefind index (optional)
steps.content: If pagefind is on PATH (brew install pagefind, or npx pagefind), run it over dist/site/. Output to dist/site/pagefind/. Soft-fails with install hint if absent.

blocks.title: build wipes its three dist trees
blocks.content: build removes dist/standalone/, dist/site/, and dist/markdown/ before rebuilding so stale files don't accumulate. Anything else you've parked under dist/ is left alone — use oku clean to wipe the entire dist/ tree.

blocks.title: oku clean
blocks.lead: Remove the dist/ tree under the current project root. Idempotent — no-op when dist/ doesn't exist. Source files and the _kit symlink are untouched.

blocks.source:
oku clean

# ✓ Removed /path/to/your-project/dist

# Second run, nothing left:
oku clean

# ✓ Nothing to clean — /path/to/your-project/dist does not exist.

items: Useful before publishing a release artifact, switching branches, or just to ensure a fresh build.
Safe to chain: oku clean && oku build.
Doesn't touch source pages, the _kit symlink, or kit.json. Only generated output.

blocks.title: oku check
blocks.lead: Lint every page-JSON in the project. Schema validation plus structural / content checks. Fast — runs in milliseconds. Designed as the oku skill's auto-verify step.

blocks.source:
oku check

# ✓ 11 page(s) clean (schema + structural + content)
#
# oku check --strict       # exit 1 on warnings too
# oku check --json         # machine-parseable output
# oku check --verbose      # also surface info-level nudges
# oku check --errors-only  # suppress warnings in the report

blocks.content: Issues land at three severities. Exit code is 1 if any error is present (or any warning under --strict); 0 otherwise.

rows: JSON shape problems, removed primitives still in use, duplicate section / heading IDs, malformed chart payloads, demo pages outside docs/reference.json, page without a title.
Prose containing round-N / vN review / fixed in round (kit documents current behaviour only). Glossary terms / ext-refs that don't resolve against kit/glossary/ / kit/extrefs/.
Code blocks without a declared language (Prism + the language pill skipped). Pages without meta.summary (manifest tooltips and llms.txt lose the one-liner).

blocks.title: Adding to the oku skill flow
blocks.content: Run oku check --strict before declaring an HTML artifact done. Use the --json mode if you want to surface findings programmatically. The linter is designed to be the fastest verification step in the auto-verify loop — no browser required.

blocks.title: oku serve
blocks.lead: Local HTTP server in the project root. Synthesizes per-page .html stubs, site-manifest.json, and llms.txt in memory on each request — source dir stays clean. Picks the first free port from 9876.

blocks.source:
oku serve

# ✓ Serving /path/to/your-project on http://localhost:9876
#   Stop with Ctrl-C.
#
#   HTML files:
#     http://localhost:9876/docs/index.html
#     http://localhost:9876/docs/reference.html
#     ...

items: Walks up from cwd to find the directory containing docs/_kit; serves from there. Run from anywhere inside the project.
First free port from 9876–9900. Caps at 9900 (if all taken, errors out).
Synthesizes /<docs>/<name>.html stubs from sibling .json or .md files on the fly; same for site-manifest.json and llms.txt. No filesystem writes.
Pagefind is not built by serve. Run oku build first if you need full-text search; serve falls back to in-page anchor search otherwise.
Opens the first HTML it finds in the default browser. Ctrl-C to stop.

content.content: Browsers apply different rules to local files than HTTP — symlink resolution, fetch, and ES module imports fail silently or behave inconsistently on file://. The local HTTP server sidesteps that. On macOS, opening a file:// URL also disables some same-origin policies that matter for the iframe sandbox in <live-snippet>. Always serve.

blocks.title: Optional flags
blocks.content:
--no-watch disables the filesystem watcher + live-reload (serve static only).
--no-search skips the background Pagefind index generation at startup. Both default to on so the dev loop is rich; opt out if you want a leaner serve.

blocks.title: Optional dependencies
blocks.lead: Two external tools the kit will use if present. Both soft-fail — install when you want the feature, skip when you don't.

cards.title: Pagefind — search index
content: Without it: search button still appears but says "Search index not found" when clicked.
With it: build adds a ~50–100 KB pagefind/ directory to dist/site/; the search button works on the built site.

cards.title: jsonschema — page validation
content: Without it: build prints a hint and skips validation.
With it: every JSON page validates against schema/page.schema.json on build; errors print field path + message. Catches malformed JSON earlier than the runtime.

blocks.title: Install + run
blocks.lead: Worth noting because they're frequently asked.

blocks.content: Two ways to invoke the CLI.

blocks.source:
uv tool install .
# Now `oku` is on PATH globally:
oku serve

blocks.content: Installs oku as a console script. The wheel packs chrome.{css,js}, schema/, glossary/, extrefs/ inside html_doc/assets/ and ships starter templates under html_doc/templates/, so init/build find everything without a git layout.

blocks.source:
uv run bin/oku serve
# Or plain python3 — both work:
python3 bin/oku serve

blocks.content: bin/oku is a thin shim that adds src/ to sys.path and runs html_doc.cli.main(). PEP 723 inline metadata pulls jsonschema into an ephemeral venv when invoked via uv.
